headline: Pony.ai showed a new electric self-driving truck and says it wants to test it in Europe, but no tests are approved.
score_reason: Product unveiling from 14 Sep with company-only claims and no approved European test; cut by 1.
importance_line: Freight carriers and European regulators are the audience, but the 70% and 30% cost figures are company claims or forecasts and no independent safety data exists.
source: Reuters, citing Pony.ai, as relayed by Streamline Feed
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by Streamline Feed, that Pony.ai, the Chinese self-driving company, unveiled an electric Level 4 heavy truck built with GAC at a Hannover trade show on 14 Sep 2026, with volume production planned later in 2026. Level 4 means the system drives without a human within set conditions; Pony.ai is talking to European governments about road tests, but no country, permit or date is named, and its cost-saving figures are company claims.
notes: Event is from 14 Sep (before 4 Oct); cost and safety figures are company claims. Article is an analysis piece quoting Reuters. Score cut 1.
